gloss: to show signs; to begin to appear; to sprout

definitions.gloss: to show signs; to begin to appear
definitions.explanation: For something not yet visible — a season, a feeling, a social change — to give its first faint indication. The subject is the thing coming into being, not the person noticing it.

examples.english: Spring is beginning to show itself.

examples.japanese: ⟦{胸|むね}→胸：00972_mune⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{不安|ふあん}→不安：00836_fuan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{兆|きざ}し⟦{始|はじ}めた→始める：00531_hajimeru⟧。
examples.english: Unease began to stir in my chest.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長|なが}い→長い：00491_nagai⟧⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{終|お}わり、⟦{野原|のはら}→野原：14417_nohara⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦あちこち→あちこち：01687_achikochi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{命|いのち}→命：02371_inochi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{兆|きざ}して⟦いた→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: The long winter had ended, and new life was beginning to appear here and there in the fields.

notes:
A literary verb, most at home in writing about nature, moods, and social currents. The related noun ⟦{兆|きざ}し→兆し：06633_kizashi⟧ (a sign, an omen) is far more common in everyday Japanese: ⟦{回復|かいふく}→回復：03812_kaifuku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{兆|きざ}し→兆し：06633_kizashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧ (signs of recovery are visible).

TRANSITIVITY:
Intransitive; the thing appearing is the subject and takes ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ (⟦{不安|ふあん}→不安：00836_fuan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{兆|きざ}す).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{兆|きざ}す: for spring to show its first signs
- ⟦{不安|ふあん}→不安：00836_fuan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{兆|きざ}す: for unease to stir
- ⟦{芽|め}→芽：02141_me⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{兆|きざ}す: for buds to start to appear

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{芽生|めば}える→芽生える：04594_mebaeru⟧: to sprout; to bud — used both of plants and of feelings, and much more common
- ⟦{現|あらわ}れる→現れる：01870_arawareru⟧: to appear — neutral and general; the thing is already visible, not merely hinted at
